title: A recurring whole marks temporal precedence without causing the next state
summary: Test whether a recurring whole orders an eligible record or event before another field without licensing a causal consequence, distinguishing temporal precedence from a causal connector and from ordinary line position.

design.mechanism: A candidate contributes temporal precedence or phase ordering while remaining semantically neutral about why the later state occurs.
design.unit: Complete candidate occurrences with independently bound event order, eligible record phase, and downstream state/consequence status.
design.contrast: Candidate-bearing earlier-phase occurrence versus matched candidate-free occurrences, with independently bound temporal order and causal relation coded separately; downstream consequence is an allowed covariate, not a required absence.
design.prediction: The candidate should predict temporal phase/order after controlling host and page, including in cases where a later state is causally dependent. A causal model predicts an independently bound causal relation, so downstream correlation alone does not distinguish or refute the precedence reading.
design.falsifier: The precedence hypothesis fails only if independently bound held cases show no candidate/order association, or if its predeclared temporal-order contrast is absent or reversed after controls. A downstream consequence correlated with candidate presence is compatible with precedence and is not by itself a falsifier; causal-versus-temporal discrimination requires cases that hold order fixed while varying causal relation, or vice versa.
design.availability: GDT269 supplies an exploratory order association but no independent semantic temporal label; event-phase and consequence endpoints are availability_unknown.
design.related: Related to IDEA000030 causal connector, but not a claim that temporal marking excludes consequences: causal dependence can follow an ordered event. The distinct target is order/phase; the causal rival requires an independent causal endpoint.
design.countermodel: A wrapper/template or field-position policy can produce earlier placement without temporal content; GDT269's position sensitivity means earlier association alone cannot identify temporal precedence.

source_evidence.quote:
The unchanged GDT267 panel contains 632 q-or-bare group occurrences. Exact
`PAGE_HOST × page` conditioning leaves 30 movable strata, 211 occurrences,
12 hosts, and all nine pages. The q/earlier association remains positive:
Mantel–Haenszel OR 1.990, conditional U +6.290, exact occurrence-level two-sided diagnostic p 0.0380, and page-cluster sign-flip p 0.0214. Seven of nine page scores are positive.

This removes the simplest alternative that GDT267 merely compared different
host vocabularies on earlier and later records. The same opaque PAGE_HOST can
occur with q and bare rendering, and q remains earlier-associated within exact
page/host strata.
